product: Deepgram — text to speech, streaming (Speak WebSocket)

source_audio.description: No audio was submitted and no request was issued: this frame is authored to Deepgram's published Speak-streaming protocol documentation, not captured from the service. The Flushed message carries no audio and no text at all.

redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted because nothing was captured. The message carries no identifier of any kind; sequence_id is an ordinal within the session, not a correlating id.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — Deepgram is not-cleared for capturing Output, so this fixture takes the documentation-derived route, which contains no Output at all

source_schema.method: The documented field set of the server-to-client Flushed message was read from the page above: type and sequence_id, the same two-field shape the Cleared message carries. The frame conforms to it. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied — only the documented field names and the literal message-type constant 'Flushed', which is interface, not expression. CONFIRMED AGAINST THE LIVE SERVICE 2026-08-15: a controlled probe of wss://api.deepgram.com/v1/speak with the SDK's shipped defaults, carrying a wrong-path control (404) and an invalid-credential control (401 at the upgrade) on the same host, received this message type with EXACTLY the field set below — so the schema half of this fixture is no longer documentation-derived: it conforms to what the service actually sends. The frame's VALUES remain our own fiction and the class stays `synthetic`; nothing of the vendor's output was stored. Only this fixture and metadata-frame were upgraded: the probe observed exactly two message types, so warning-frame and audio-linear16-16khz keep their documentation-derived class — the Warning frame and the error paths were never exercised.

notes: The end-of-utterance terminator DeepgramSpeechSynthesizer stops on. Two documented fields, both modelled — this frame is small because the vendor's is, not because it was trimmed. Deliberately still a recording rather than an inline literal: it is the frame whose type value decides when the stream ends, so it is exactly the payload that should be reviewable next to its source_schema instead of buried in a fake server. What this artifact is worth: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, whereas a capture is what it actually sent on one day. Re-read the source_schema URL first when this suite starts failing; the page publishes no revision marker.
